title: Chien-Shiung Wu and the Broken Mirror of Nature
summary: Physics assumed nature treats left and right with identical symmetry. At temperatures near absolute zero, an extraordinary Chinese-American experimentalist aligned radioactive Cobalt-60 nuclei and proved that the universe is fundamentally left-handed.
keywords: Chien-Shiung Wu and the Broken Mirror of Nature
Discovery of Parity Violation in Weak Nuclear Interactions
full_text:
In 1956 CE, the frontiers of human understanding were transformed through the indomitable persistence of Chien-Shiung Wu.

At the time, the reigning scientific establishment in the field of Experimental Nuclear Physics was constrained by orthodox paradigms that could no longer account for emerging experimental anomalies. While many researchers looked past these discrepancies or dismissed them as instrument artifacts, Chien-Shiung Wu recognized that the anomaly was itself a beacon pointing toward an undiscovered law of nature.

Working from primary documentation recorded in *Experimental Test of Parity Conservation in Beta Decay (Physical Review, 1957)* (Vol. 105, Issue 4, pp. 1413–1415), the breakthrough emerged through painstaking methodology. Every alternative hypothesis was systematically tested, isolated, and eliminated under rigorous controls.

Physics assumed nature treats left and right with identical symmetry. At temperatures near absolute zero, an extraordinary Chinese-American experimentalist aligned radioactive Cobalt-60 nuclei and proved that the universe is fundamentally left-handed.

The discovery of Discovery of Parity Violation in Weak Nuclear Interactions did not merely answer a localized puzzle; it triggered a profound paradigm shift across Experimental Nuclear Physics. Today, its principles form the bedrock of modern empirical science, reminding every student that progress is forged when courageous curiosity meets disciplined observation.
